grammarRules.title: Use plural nouns after numbers greater than one
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa sustantivos en plural después de números mayores que uno
grammarRules.explanation: Use a plural count noun after two, three, four, five, many or several. This matcher covers a reviewed set of regular nouns.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa un sustantivo contable en plural después de two, three, four, five, many o several. Este patrón cubre un conjunto revisado de sustantivos regulares.
exceptions: Irregular plurals such as children and people are not handled.
Uncountable nouns such as equipment and information do not take this pattern.

negativeCases.reason: Singular after one is correct.
Equipment is uncountable in this meaning.

practice.promptEs: Tengo tres ___ (robot).

practice.prompt: Write a sentence with two sensors.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración con two sensors.

searchTerms: Use plural nouns after numbers greater than one
Usa sustantivos en plural después de números mayores que uno

grammarRules.title: Use there is with one singular count noun
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa there is con un sustantivo contable singular
grammarRules.explanation: Use there is before a/an + singular count noun. Use there are with plural nouns.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa there is antes de a/an + un sustantivo contable singular. Usa there are con sustantivos plurales.
examples: There is a robot in the lab.
There are two robots in the lab.

examplesBilingual.en: There is a robot in the lab.
examplesBilingual.es: Hay un robot en el laboratorio.

examplesBilingual.en: There are two robots in the lab.
examplesBilingual.es: Hay dos robots en el laboratorio.

incorrect: There are a robot in the lab.
exceptions: There are is correct with plural noun phrases.
There is also introduces uncountable nouns: There is some equipment.

negativeCases.reason: Plural agreement is correct.
Equipment is uncountable.

practice.promptEs: ___ un sensor sobre la mesa.

practice.prompt: Describe one object using There is.
practice.promptEs: Describe un objeto usando There is.

searchTerms: Use there is with one singular count noun
Usa there is con un sustantivo contable singular

grammarRules.title: Use the base verb after does in questions
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el verbo base después de does en preguntas
grammarRules.explanation: In a present-simple question with does, the main verb stays in its base form.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En una pregunta en presente simple con does, el verbo principal queda en forma base.
examples: Does the robot use a sensor?

examplesBilingual.en: Does the robot use a sensor?

exceptions: Statements correctly use third-person -s: She works here.
Questions with be do not use does: Is she ready.

negativeCases.reason: A statement correctly uses works.
The question is already correct.

practice.promptEs: ¿Él ___ aquí?

practice.prompt: Ask a present-simple question with does.
practice.promptEs: Haz una pregunta en presente simple con does.

searchTerms: Use the base verb after does in questions
Usa el verbo base después de does en preguntas

grammarRules.title: Use the base verb after a modal
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el verbo base después de un modal
grammarRules.explanation: After can, could, should, must and will, use the base form of the main verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Después de can, could, should, must y will, usa la forma base del verbo principal.
exceptions: The modal itself does not take -s: He can, not He cans.
Have to and ought to use different patterns.

negativeCases.reason: Modal + base verb is correct.
This is not a modal construction.

practice.promptEs: Él puede ___ inglés.

practice.prompt: Write a sentence with should + a base verb.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración con should + verbo base.

searchTerms: Use the base verb after a modal
Usa el verbo base después de un modal

grammarRules.title: Use the base verb after did
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el verbo base después de did
grammarRules.explanation: In past-simple questions with did, use the base form of the main verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En preguntas en pasado simple con did, usa la forma base del verbo principal.
examples: Did you go to the lab?

examplesBilingual.en: Did you go to the lab?

incorrect: Did you went to the lab?
exceptions: Affirmative past statements use past forms: She built the robot.
Current matching focuses on questions, not every negative construction.

negativeCases.text: Did you go to the lab?
negativeCases.reason: Did + base verb is correct.

negativeCases.text: She went to the lab yesterday.
negativeCases.reason: Affirmative past simple is correct.

practice.promptEs: ¿Fuiste a clase?

practice.prompt: Ask a question about yesterday with Did you...
practice.promptEs: Haz una pregunta sobre ayer con Did you...

searchTerms: Use the base verb after did
Usa el verbo base después de did

grammarRules.title: Use an -ing form after be in the present continuous
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa la forma -ing después de be en presente continuo
grammarRules.explanation: For an action happening now, use am/is/are + the -ing form of the main verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Para una acción que ocurre ahora, usa am/is/are + la forma -ing del verbo principal.
exceptions: Be + adjective/noun is valid: I am ready; They are students.
Stative verbs are not normally continuous in common meanings: I know the answer.

negativeCases.reason: Be + adjective is correct.
Know is stative in this meaning.

practice.promptEs: Ella está ___ ahora.

practice.prompt: Describe what someone is doing now.
practice.promptEs: Describe qué está haciendo alguien ahora.

matcher.pattern: \b(I am|he is|she is|it is|we are|they are|you are)\s+(work|teach|build|study|learn|write|read|use)\b

searchTerms: Use an -ing form after be in the present continuous
Usa la forma -ing después de be en presente continuo

grammarRules.title: Use the first conditional for realistic future possibilities
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el primer condicional para posibilidades futuras reales
grammarRules.explanation: Use if + present simple followed by will/can/may + base verb for a realistic future condition and result.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa if + presente simple seguido de will/can/may + verbo base para expresar una condición futura realista y su resultado.
examples: If the sensor fails, we will replace it.
If we finish early, we can test the robot.

examplesBilingual.en: If the sensor fails, we will replace it.
examplesBilingual.es: Si falla el sensor, lo reemplazaremos.

examplesBilingual.en: If we finish early, we can test the robot.
examplesBilingual.es: Si terminamos temprano, podemos probar el robot.

incorrect: If the sensor will fail, we will replace it.
exceptions: Will is normally not used in the if-clause of this pattern.
Other conditional meanings use different structures.

negativeCases.text: If it rains, we will stay inside.
negativeCases.reason: Correct first conditional.

practice.prompt: Complete: If the sensor ___ (fail), we will stop.
practice.promptEs: Completa: If the sensor ___, nos detendremos.

searchTerms: Use the first conditional for realistic future possibilities
Usa el primer condicional para posibilidades futuras reales

grammarRules.title: Choose connectors by meaning and clause structure
grammarRules.titleEs: Elige conectores según el significado y la estructura
grammarRules.explanation: Although introduces a contrast clause; however links ideas across sentence boundaries; because introduces a reason.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Although introduce una oración de contraste; however enlaza ideas entre oraciones; because introduce una razón.
examples: Although the task was difficult, we finished it.
The task was difficult. However, we finished it.

examplesBilingual.en: Although the task was difficult, we finished it.
examplesBilingual.es: Aunque la tarea fue difícil, la terminamos.

examplesBilingual.en: The task was difficult. However, we finished it.
examplesBilingual.es: La tarea fue difícil. Sin embargo, la terminamos.

incorrect: Although the task was difficult, but we finished it.
exceptions: Punctuation depends on clause structure.
But is not universally wrong; it is redundant in this although...but construction.

negativeCases.text: Although it was late, we continued.
negativeCases.reason: Correct contrast clause.

practice.promptEs: Une dos ideas usando although.

searchTerms: Choose connectors by meaning and clause structure
Elige conectores según el significado y la estructura

grammarRules.title: Support a claim with reasons and qualified evidence
grammarRules.titleEs: Sustenta una afirmación con razones y evidencia matizada
grammarRules.explanation: A clear argument distinguishes a claim, supporting reason, evidence and limitation; avoid presenting correlation as proof of causation.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Un argumento claro distingue afirmación, razón, evidencia y limitación; evita presentar correlación como prueba de causalidad.
examples: The results suggest that the method may improve retention, although the sample was small.
One limitation is that the study included only one class.

examplesBilingual.en: The results suggest that the method may improve retention, although the sample was small.
examplesBilingual.es: Los resultados sugieren que el método podría mejorar la retención, aunque la muestra era pequeña.

examplesBilingual.en: One limitation is that the study included only one class.
examplesBilingual.es: Una limitación es que el estudio incluyó una sola clase.

incorrect: The results prove the method always works, based only on one small class.
exceptions: The strength of wording must match the evidence.
May, might, suggest and indicate express different degrees of certainty.

negativeCases.text: The results may suggest an improvement.
negativeCases.reason: Qualified wording is appropriate when evidence is limited.

practice.prompt: Write a claim with a qualification and a supporting reason.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una afirmación con matización y una razón de apoyo.

searchTerms: Support a claim with reasons and qualified evidence
Sustenta una afirmación con razones y evidencia matizada

grammarRules.title: Maintain cohesion with reference and lexical links
grammarRules.titleEs: Mantén la cohesión mediante referencias y enlaces léxicos
grammarRules.explanation: Use pronouns, repeated key terms, synonyms and transition signals so readers can identify what each expression refers to.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa pronombres, términos clave, sinónimos y conectores para que el lector identifique los referentes.
examples: The prototype failed the first test. This result led us to redesign the sensor.
The team revised the plan; consequently, the launch date changed.

examplesBilingual.en: The prototype failed the first test. This result led us to redesign the sensor.
examplesBilingual.es: El prototipo falló la primera prueba. Este resultado nos llevó a rediseñar el sensor.

examplesBilingual.en: The team revised the plan; consequently, the launch date changed.
examplesBilingual.es: El equipo revisó el plan; en consecuencia, cambió la fecha de lanzamiento.

incorrect: The prototype failed. It was changed. This did that.
exceptions: Repetition can be useful for clarity; avoid ambiguous synonyms.
Transition signals express different logical relationships and are not interchangeable.

negativeCases.text: The team revised the plan; consequently, the launch date changed.
negativeCases.reason: The transition clearly expresses a result.

practice.prompt: Revise a paragraph to clarify references and logical links.
practice.promptEs: Revisa un párrafo para aclarar referencias y relaciones lógicas.

searchTerms: Maintain cohesion with reference and lexical links
Mantén la cohesión mediante referencias y enlaces léxicos

grammarRules.title: Basic question word order
grammarRules.explanation: In many present-simple questions, use do/does + subject + base verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En muchas preguntas en presente simple, usa do/does + sujeto + verbo base.
exceptions: Questions with be invert be and subject: Are you ready?
After does, use the base verb.

negativeCases.reason: Correct do-support.
Be-questions do not use do/does.

practice.promptEs: Ordena: where / do / you / work

practice.prompt: Ask a classmate where they live.
practice.promptEs: Pregunta a un compañero dónde vive.

grammarRules.title: Use in/on/at for common time expressions
grammarRules.explanation: Use at for clock times, on for days and dates, and in for months, years and parts of the day.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa at para horas, on para días y fechas e in para meses, años y partes del día.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

exceptions: Fixed expressions can be idiomatic: at night, in the morning.
Prepositions are not interchangeable across all time phrases.

negativeCases.reason: Correct clock-time phrase.
Correct month phrase.

practice.promptEs: La clase empieza ___ las nueve.

practice.prompt: Write a sentence with on + a day.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración con on + un día.

searchTerms: Use in/on/at for common time expressions

grammarRules.title: Use common prepositions of place
grammarRules.explanation: In, on, under, next to and between describe different spatial relationships.
grammarRules.explanationEs: In, on, under, next to y between describen relaciones espaciales diferentes.
examples: The sensor is under the table.
The lab is next to the library.
incorrect: The sensor is between the table

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

examplesBilingual.en: The sensor is under the table.
examplesBilingual.es: El sensor está debajo de la mesa.

examplesBilingual.en: The lab is next to the library.
examplesBilingual.es: El laboratorio está al lado de la biblioteca.

exceptions: In, on, under, next to and between encode different spatial relations.
Choose a preposition based on the intended physical relationship.

negativeCases.text: The sensor is under the table.
negativeCases.reason: Correct spatial relation.

negativeCases.text: The lab is next to the library.
negativeCases.reason: Correct spatial relation.

practice.promptEs: El libro está ___ la mesa (superficie).
Describe dónde están dos objetos.

grammarRules.title: Build the present perfect
grammarRules.explanation: Use have/has + past participle for experiences and past actions connected to now.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa have/has + participio para experiencias y acciones pasadas relacionadas con el presente.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

exceptions: Use past simple with finished past-time expressions such as yesterday or last week.
Have/has must be followed by a past participle.

negativeCases.reason: Correct present perfect.
Correct past simple with a finished time.

practice.promptEs: Ellos han ___ el circuito.
Escribe sobre un logro reciente.

grammarRules.title: Basic passive voice
grammarRules.explanation: Use be + past participle when the action or result is more important than the agent.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa be + participio cuando la acción o el resultado importa más que quién la realiza.
examples: The robot was designed by students.
The project is tested every week.
incorrect: The robot was design by students.

examplesBilingual.en: The robot was designed by students.
examplesBilingual.es: El robot fue diseñado por estudiantes.

examplesBilingual.en: The project is tested every week.
examplesBilingual.es: El proyecto se prueba cada semana.

exceptions: Active voice is correct when the agent is the focus: Students designed the robot.
Progressive passive uses be + being + past participle.

negativeCases.text: The robot was designed by students.
negativeCases.reason: Correct passive voice.
Correct active voice.

practice.promptEs: El circuito fue ___ ayer.

practice.prompt: Describe how a device is made.
practice.promptEs: Describe cómo se fabrica un dispositivo.

grammarRules.title: Use statement word order in indirect questions
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa orden afirmativo en preguntas indirectas
grammarRules.explanation: Indirect questions use subject + verb order after Could you tell me.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Las preguntas indirectas usan sujeto + verbo después de Could you tell me.
examples: Could you tell me where the lab is?
Do you know what the task is?
incorrect: Could you tell me where is the lab?

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

examplesBilingual.en: Could you tell me where the lab is?
Do you know what the task is?

exceptions: Direct questions keep inversion: Where is the lab?
Embedded yes/no questions commonly use if or whether.

negativeCases.text: Could you tell me where the lab is?
negativeCases.reason: Correct embedded question order.
Correct direct question inversion.

practice.prompt: Could you tell me / where / the lab / is?
practice.promptEs: Ordena la pregunta indirecta.

practice.prompt: Ask politely where a room is.
practice.promptEs: Pregunta cortésmente dónde queda un salón.

searchTerms: Use statement word order in indirect questions
Usa orden afirmativo en preguntas indirectas

grammarRules.title: Form present simple questions with do/does
grammarRules.titleEs: Forma preguntas en presente simple con do/does
grammarRules.explanation: Use do/does before the subject; use the base verb after does.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa do/does antes del sujeto y el verbo base después de does.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

exceptions: Use do with I/you/we/they and does with he/she/it.
After does, use the base verb; be-questions do not use do/does.

negativeCases.reason: Correct does + base verb.
Correct present-simple statement.

practice.promptEs: ¿Él ___ aquí?
Haz una pregunta sobre una rutina diaria.

searchTerms: Form present simple questions with do/does
Forma preguntas en presente simple con do/does

grammarRules.title: Form regular plural nouns
grammarRules.explanation: Most countable nouns form the plural with -s or -es.
grammarRules.explanationEs: La mayoría de sustantivos contables forman el plural con -s o -es.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

exceptions: Nouns ending in s, sh, ch, x or z often take -es.
Consonant + y changes to -ies; some plurals are irregular.
Uncountable nouns usually do not take a plural in their usual meaning.

negativeCases.reason: Correct regular plural.
Correct irregular plural.

practice.promptEs: Tres ___ están listos.

practice.prompt: Name three objects in your classroom.
practice.promptEs: Nombra tres objetos de tu salón.

grammarRules.title: Distinguish general plural nouns from specific nouns
grammarRules.titleEs: Distingue plurales generales de nombres específicos
grammarRules.explanation: Plural countable nouns can appear without the when speaking generally; the signals a specific group.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los plurales contables pueden ir sin the en sentido general; the identifica un grupo específico.
examples: The robots in this lab are new.
incorrect: The robots can help people (general meaning)

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

examplesBilingual.es: Los robots pueden ayudar a las personas.

examplesBilingual.en: The robots in this lab are new.
examplesBilingual.es: Los robots de este laboratorio son nuevos.

exceptions: The is appropriate for a specific group: The robots in this lab.
General singular count nouns usually need an article.

negativeCases.reason: Correct general plural.

negativeCases.text: The robots in this lab are new.
negativeCases.reason: Correct specific group.

practice.prompt: ___ robots can help in dangerous places.
practice.promptEs: ___ robots pueden ayudar en lugares peligrosos.

practice.prompt: Compare a general statement with a specific group.
practice.promptEs: Compara una afirmación general con un grupo específico.

searchTerms: Distinguish general plural nouns from specific nouns
Distingue plurales generales de nombres específicos

grammarRules.title: Use object pronouns after verbs and prepositions
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa pronombres de objeto después de verbos y preposiciones
grammarRules.explanation: Use me, him, her, us and them as objects, not I/he/she/we/they.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa me, him, her, us y them como objetos, no I/he/she/we/they.

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

exceptions: Use subject pronouns before a verb: She helped me, not Her helped me.
Object pronouns follow verbs and prepositions.

negativeCases.reason: Correct object pronoun.
Correct object pronoun after a preposition.

practice.promptEs: El profesor me ayudó.

practice.prompt: Write a sentence using him, her or them.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración con him, her o them.

searchTerms: Use object pronouns after verbs and prepositions
Usa pronombres de objeto después de verbos y preposiciones

grammarRules.title: Use since for a starting point and for for a duration
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa since para punto inicial y for para duración
grammarRules.explanation: Use since + starting point and for + duration in common present-perfect contexts.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa since + punto inicial y for + duración.
examples: I have worked here for five years.
incorrect: I have worked here since five years

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

examplesBilingual.en: I have worked here for five years.
examplesBilingual.es: He trabajado aquí durante cinco años.

exceptions: Since introduces a starting point; for introduces a duration.
Past simple is often used with a finished period.

negativeCases.text: I have worked here for five years.
negativeCases.reason: Correct duration phrase.
Correct starting point.

practice.promptEs: Estudio inglés ___ 2024.

practice.prompt: Write a sentence with for + duration.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración con for + duración.

searchTerms: Use since for a starting point and for for a duration
Usa since para punto inicial y for para duración

grammarRules.title: Use although and however appropriately
grammarRules.explanation: Although introduces a subordinate contrast clause; however often links clauses with punctuation.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Although introduce una subordinada concesiva; however suele conectar oraciones con puntuación apropiada.
examples: Although it was hard, we finished.
It was hard. However, we finished.
incorrect: Although it was hard, but we finished

review.reason: Needs dedicated implementation and positive/negative regression tests before activation.

examplesBilingual.en: Although it was hard, we finished.
It was hard. However, we finished.

exceptions: Do not normally add but to the same clause introduced by although.
However commonly needs punctuation separating clauses.

negativeCases.text: Although it was hard, we finished.
negativeCases.reason: Correct although clause.

negativeCases.text: It was hard. However, we finished.
negativeCases.reason: Correct however punctuation.

practice.promptEs: ___ era tarde, continuamos.

practice.prompt: Join two contrasting ideas with although.
practice.promptEs: Une dos ideas contrastantes con although.

grammarRules.title: First Conditional
grammarRules.explanation: Use if + present simple, will + base verb for a real future possibility.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa if + presente simple, will + verbo base para una posibilidad futura real.
examples: If we practise, we will improve.
If the sensor fails, we will stop.
incorrect: If we will practise, we will improve.

examplesBilingual.en: If we practise, we will improve.
If the sensor fails, we will stop.
examplesBilingual.es: Si falla el sensor, nos detendremos.

exceptions: In the first conditional, the if-clause normally uses present simple, not will.
Other conditional meanings use other structures.

negativeCases.text: If we practise, we will improve.
negativeCases.reason: Correct first conditional.

negativeCases.text: If it rains, we will stay inside.
negativeCases.reason: Correct first conditional.

practice.prompt: If the sensor ___ (fail), we will stop.
practice.promptEs: Si falla el sensor, nos detendremos.

practice.prompt: Write a realistic if-clause and result.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una condición realista y su resultado.

grammarRules.title: Use subject pronouns before verbs
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa pronombres sujeto antes de los verbos
grammarRules.explanation: Use I, you, he, she, it, we and they as the subject of a clause. Subject pronouns normally appear before the verb.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa I, you, he, she, it, we y they como sujeto de una oración. Los pronombres sujeto normalmente aparecen antes del verbo.
exceptions: You has the same form for singular and plural subjects.
It is used for things, animals when appropriate, weather and time.
Object pronouns follow verbs or prepositions: She helped me.

negativeCases.reason: I is the correct subject pronoun.
Me is correctly used as the object.
They is the correct plural subject.

practice.promptEs: ___ son estudiantes. (They/Them)

practice.prompt: Write one sentence with he and one with they.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración con he y otra con they.

grammarRules.implementationReadiness: content complete; implementation and contrastive tests pending
searchTerms: Usa pronombres sujeto antes de los verbos

grammarRules.title: Capitalize the pronoun I
grammarRules.explanation: The subject pronoun I is always capitalized.
grammarRules.explanationEs: El pronombre I siempre se escribe con mayúscula.
exceptions: The pronoun I is always capitalized, including I'm.
Other first-person forms such as me and my are not capitalized unless they begin a sentence.

negativeCases.reason: I is correctly capitalized.
My and me are not capitalized in the middle of a sentence.

practice.promptEs: Corrige: i am ready.

practice.prompt: Write a sentence beginning with I.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración que comience con I.

grammarRules.title: Spell teacher correctly
grammarRules.explanation: The word is spelled teacher.
grammarRules.explanationEs: La palabra se escribe teacher.
exceptions: This spelling record covers the noun teacher, not every word with a similar sound.
Do not change a correctly spelled word just because another variant exists.

negativeCases.reason: Teacher is spelled correctly.
Teacher is spelled correctly.

practice.promptEs: Completa: teac___ (una persona que enseña).
Escribe una oración con teacher.

grammarRules.title: Use an article before a singular job
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa un artículo antes de una profesión singular
grammarRules.explanation: Use a/an before a singular countable job noun.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa a/an antes de un sustantivo contable singular que indique una profesión.
exceptions: A singular countable job noun normally needs a/an after be.
Plural jobs do not take a/an: They are teachers.

negativeCases.reason: Correct article before a singular job.
Plural job noun correctly has no a/an.

practice.promptEs: Ella es ___ ingeniera.
Describe tu profesión usando a/an.

searchTerms: Use an article before a singular job
Usa un artículo antes de una profesión singular

grammarRules.title: Choose a or an by sound
grammarRules.titleEs: Elige a o an según el sonido
grammarRules.explanation: Use an before a vowel sound, and a before a consonant sound.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa an antes de un sonido vocálico y a antes de un sonido consonántico.
exceptions: Choose by the first sound, not the first letter: a university, an hour.
Plural nouns and uncountable nouns do not normally use a/an.

negativeCases.reason: Correct vowel sound.
University begins with a /juː/ consonant sound.

practice.promptEs: ___ hora
___ herramienta útil

grammarRules.title: Match be to the subject
grammarRules.explanation: Use am with I, is with he/she/it, and are with you/we/they.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa am con I, is con he/she/it y are con you/we/they.
exceptions: Am pairs with I; is with he/she/it and singular noun phrases; are with you/we/they and plural noun phrases.
Contractions are valid: I'm, she's, they're.

negativeCases.reason: Correct I + am.
Correct plural subject + are.
The contraction is valid.

practice.promptEs: Ellos están listos.

practice.prompt: Write one sentence with I am and one with they are.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración con I am y otra con they are.

grammarRules.title: Avoid accidental repeated connectors
grammarRules.explanation: Do not repeat the same connector twice in a row unless quoting or deliberately repeating it.
grammarRules.explanationEs: No repitas el mismo conector dos veces seguidas, salvo que estés citando o repitiendo deliberadamente.
examples: I teach robotics and I enjoy it.
She studies English and practises every day.
incorrect: I teach and and enjoy it.

examplesBilingual.en: I teach robotics and I enjoy it.
She studies English and practises every day.
examplesBilingual.es: Ella estudia inglés y practica todos los días.

exceptions: Repeated and can be deliberate for emphasis or lists; do not remove it automatically without context.
A sentence may contain multiple conjunctions when they connect different clauses.

negativeCases.text: I teach robotics and I enjoy it.
negativeCases.reason: The connector is not accidentally repeated.

negativeCases.text: I bought pens, books and sensors.
negativeCases.reason: A list with and is correct.

practice.prompt: Edit only an accidental repeated connector.
practice.promptEs: Corrige solo un conector repetido por accidente.

practice.prompt: Join two related ideas with and.
practice.promptEs: Une dos ideas relacionadas con and.

grammarRules.title: Use the base verb after do not and does not
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el verbo base después de do not y does not
grammarRules.explanation: After do not, does not, don't or doesn't, use the base form of the main verb. Do not add -s after doesn't.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Después de do not, does not, don't o doesn't, usa la forma base del verbo principal. No añadas -s después de doesn't.
examples: I don't build robots every day.

examplesBilingual.en: I don't build robots every day.
examplesBilingual.es: No construyo robots todos los días.

exceptions: This rule covers a reviewed list of common verbs; it is not a complete detector for every verb.
Do not change affirmative statements such as She works on Sundays.

negativeCases.reason: Doesn't is followed by the base verb.
Affirmative third-person singular correctly uses -s.
Don't + base verb is correct.

practice.promptEs: Él no ___ los viernes.

practice.prompt: Write a negative sentence with doesn't + a base verb.
practice.promptEs: Escribe una oración negativa con doesn't + verbo base.

grammarRules.title: Use the base verb after did not
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el verbo base después de did not
grammarRules.explanation: After didn't or did not, use the base form of the main verb, not the past form.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Después de didn't o did not, usa la forma base del verbo principal, no la forma de pasado.
examples: I didn't go to school yesterday.
She did not build the robot.

examplesBilingual.en: I didn't go to school yesterday.
She did not build the robot.

incorrect: I didn't went to school yesterday.
She did not built the robot.
exceptions: The rule covers a reviewed set of common regular and irregular verbs.
Affirmative past statements correctly use the past form: She built the robot.

negativeCases.text: I didn't go to school yesterday.
negativeCases.reason: Didn't + base verb is correct.
The affirmative past form is correct.
Did is the main verb here, not an auxiliary followed by a past form.

grammarRules.title: Do not use to after a modal verb
grammarRules.titleEs: No uses to después de un verbo modal
grammarRules.explanation: After can, could, should, must or will, use the base verb without to.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Después de can, could, should, must o will, usa el verbo base sin to.
incorrect: I can to build a robot.
We should to check the code.
exceptions: Want to and have to are valid patterns; this rule does not apply to them.
This rule only covers the listed modals and a reviewed list of verbs.

negativeCases.reason: Modal + base verb is correct.

grammarRules.title: Use the main verb without be for agree, understand and know
grammarRules.titleEs: Usa el verbo principal sin be con agree, understand y know
grammarRules.explanation: In simple present statements, use I agree, I understand and I know. Do not put am before these main verbs.
grammarRules.explanationEs: En presente simple, usa I agree, I understand e I know. No pongas am antes de estos verbos principales.
exceptions: This narrow rule covers only I am + agree/understand/know; it does not claim to cover every use of be.
I am a teacher is correct because teacher is a noun.

negativeCases.reason: The main verb agree is used directly.
Be + noun is correct.
Be + -ing forms the present continuous.

grammarRules.title: Position of frequency adverbs
grammarRules.titleEs: Posición de los adverbios de frecuencia
grammarRules.explanation: Frequency adverbs usually go before the main verb, but after be.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Los adverbios de frecuencia suelen ir antes del verbo principal, pero después de be.

examplesBilingual.es: Los adverbios de frecuencia suelen ir antes del verbo principal, pero después de be.

exceptions: With be, the adverb normally follows be: She is often busy.
Adverbs can appear at the beginning for emphasis in some contexts.

grammarRules.title: Subject and object pronouns
grammarRules.explanation: Use subject pronouns before a verb and object pronouns after a verb or preposition.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa pronombres de sujeto antes del verbo y pronombres de objeto después de un verbo o preposición.

examplesBilingual.es: Usa pronombres de sujeto antes del verbo y pronombres de objeto después de un verbo o preposición.

grammarRules.title: Possessive adjectives
grammarRules.explanation: Use my, your, his, her, its, our and their before a noun to show possession.

grammarRules.title: Some and any
grammarRules.explanation: Some is common in affirmative statements; any is common in negatives and questions. Usage depends on meaning and context.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Some es común en afirmaciones; any, en negaciones y preguntas. El uso depende del significado y del contexto.

examplesBilingual.es: Some es común en afirmaciones; any, en negaciones y preguntas. El uso depende del significado y del contexto.

exceptions: Some is also natural in offers and requests: Would you like some water?
Any can mean cualquiera in affirmative sentences.

grammarRules.title: Much and many
grammarRules.explanation: Use many with plural countable nouns and much with uncountable nouns, especially in questions and negatives.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa many con sustantivos contables plurales y much con incontables, especialmente en preguntas y negaciones.
examples: How much time do we have?

grammarRules.title: Present simple and present continuous
grammarRules.explanation: Use present simple for routines and facts; present continuous for actions happening now or temporary situations.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa presente simple para rutinas y hechos; presente continuo para acciones que ocurren ahora o situaciones temporales.

examplesBilingual.es: Usa presente simple para rutinas y hechos; presente continuo para acciones que ocurren ahora o situaciones temporales.

incorrect: I am teaching robotics every week (for a permanent routine).
I teach now (for an action happening at this moment).
exceptions: Some verbs of state are not normally used in continuous forms; temporary repeated actions can use continuous.

negativeCases.reason: This is an example of the intended pattern and must not be flagged as an error.

grammarRules.title: Common irregular past forms
grammarRules.explanation: Many common verbs have irregular past forms, such as go/went, build/built and teach/taught.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Muchos verbos frecuentes tienen pasado irregular, como go/went, build/built y teach/taught.

grammarRules.titleEs: Pasado simple con expresiones de tiempo terminado
grammarRules.explanation: Use past simple with finished times such as yesterday, last week and in 2024.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa pasado simple con tiempos terminados como yesterday, last week e in 2024.

grammarRules.title: Present perfect for life experience

grammarRules.title: For and since
grammarRules.explanation: Use for with a duration and since with a starting point.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa for con una duración y since con un punto de inicio.

grammarRules.title: First conditional
grammarRules.explanation: Use if + present simple and will + base verb for a realistic future possibility.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Usa if + presente simple y will + verbo base para una posibilidad futura realista.
examples: If we practise, we will improve.
If the sensor fails, we will check the circuit.

exceptions: Will can appear in an if-clause in special meanings such as willingness; the basic rule is not universal.

grammarRules.title: Connectors for reason and result
grammarRules.explanation: Because introduces a reason; so and therefore introduce a result, with different sentence structures and punctuation.
grammarRules.explanationEs: Because introduce una razón; so y therefore introducen un resultado, con estructuras y puntuación diferentes.
examples: I practise because I want to improve.
I was tired, so I rested.
The test failed; therefore, we checked the code.

The test failed; therefore, we checked the code.

I was tired, therefore I rested.
exceptions: Punctuation and clause structure matter; therefore is not interchangeable with so in every position.
